summary: Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Harvard and Oxford, completing his doctorate under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held positions at Middlebury College, Harvard University (1980–1991), and Boston University (1990–2024).

Mallica Kumbera Landrus specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. As of 2026, she holds appointments as Associate Professor of Indian Art and Keeper of Eastern Art at the Ashmolean Museum, affiliated with the University of Oxford and Wolfson College.
Mamata Dash is an Indology scholar who was educated at Ravenshaw Girls' High School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami was a historian, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki, he earned a doctorate and served at Kobe University (1971), Kyoto University (1965–2001, professor from 1984), and Otani University (2003).
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as Co-ordinator of DSA Sanskrit at Jadavpur University (attested 2003) and as Secretary of the Asiatic Society.

Manabu Asano is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued doctoral studies at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020) and became a researcher at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

Manasi Dilip Nadkarni works in linguistics and Indology. She conducted doctoral research under Shyam Sundar Bhattacharya and has been affiliated with the Asiatic Society as a Research Scholar/Fellow (attested 2026).

Manfred B. Steger works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa and Rutgers University, he held professorships at Illinois State University, RMIT University, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (2011–2016).

Manfred Mayrhofer was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz. He served as a professor at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

Manfred Taube was a scholar of Tibetology and Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig University under Friedrich Weller and served as Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology at Leipzig University starting in 1991.

Manshi Kiyozawa was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa. He served at Kyoto Prefectural Rakuhoku High School and became the founding president of Otani University (1901–1902).
Manu Leumann was an Indologist and linguist who held academic posts at the University of Munich (~1922–1927) and the University of Zurich (~1927–1959).

Marc Aurel Stein was an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. His posts included Principal of Oriental College, Principal of Aliah University, and officer positions in the Archaeological Survey of India.
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2016 under the supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein, having also studied with Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Cohen was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He held long-term posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1919–1954), the University of Paris, and the newspaper L'Humanité (~1944–1974).

Marcel Granet was a Sinologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. He held professorships at INALCO, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises.

Marcel Griaule was a French scholar who studied at INALCO and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Marcel Mauss and Marcel Cohen. He later held an academic post at the University of Paris (~1942–1956).

Marcel Mauss studied under Émile Durkheim, Sylvain Lévi, Antoine Meillet, and others across Bordeaux, the EPHE, and Dutch and British universities. He held chairs at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1901–1940) and the Collège de France (1931–1940).

Marcelle Lalou was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, Paul Pelliot, and Jean Przyluski. She taught at the EPHE (1938–1963).
